# 1 Kings Chapter 21 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** There was a man named Naboth from Jezreel who owned a vineyard next to the palace of King Ahab of Samaria.
**2** Ahab said to Naboth, "Let me have your vineyard so I can use it as a vegetable garden — it's right next to my palace. I'll give you a better vineyard in exchange, or if you prefer, I'll pay you whatever it's worth."
**3** Naboth replied, "The LORD forbid that I should give you my family's inheritance."
**4** Ahab went home angry and sulking over Naboth's refusal. He lay on his bed, turned his face to the wall, and refused to eat.
**5** His wife Jezebel came in and asked, "What's the matter? Why won't you eat?"
**6** He told her, "I asked Naboth the Jezreelite to sell me his vineyard or let me trade him a better one, and he said, 'I won't give you my vineyard.'"
**7** Jezebel said, "Is this how the king of Israel acts? Get up! Eat something and cheer up. I'll get you Naboth's vineyard."
**8** She wrote letters in Ahab's name, sealed them with his royal seal, and sent them to the elders and leading citizens of Naboth's town.
**9** In the letters she wrote: "Announce a day of fasting and give Naboth a prominent seat.
**10** Then seat two scoundrels across from him and have them testify that he cursed God and the king. Then take him out and stone him to death."
**11** The elders and leaders of the town did exactly what Jezebel instructed in her letters.
**12** They proclaimed a fast and gave Naboth a seat of honor.
**13** Two scoundrels sat across from him and publicly accused him: "Naboth has cursed God and the king!" They dragged him outside the town and stoned him to death.
**14** They sent word to Jezebel: "Naboth has been stoned. He's dead."
**15** When Jezebel got the news, she told Ahab, "Get up and take possession of Naboth's vineyard — the one he refused to sell you. Naboth is no longer alive. He's dead."
**16** When Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, he went down to take possession of the vineyard.
**17** Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite:
**18** "Go down and confront King Ahab of Israel in Samaria. He is in Naboth's vineyard, taking possession of it.
**19** Tell him, 'This is what the LORD says: Have you murdered a man and stolen his property?' Then tell him, 'This is what the LORD says: In the very place where dogs licked up Naboth's blood, dogs will lick up your blood — yes, yours!'"
**20** Ahab said to Elijah, "So you've found me, my enemy!" "I have," Elijah replied. "You have sold yourself to do evil in the LORD's sight.
**21** I am going to bring disaster on you. I will wipe out your descendants and cut off every male in your family — slave or free — in Israel.
**22** I will make your dynasty like Jeroboam son of Nebat's and like Baasha son of Ahijah's, because you have provoked my anger and led Israel into sin.
**23** And about Jezebel, the LORD says: 'Dogs will devour Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.'
**24** Dogs will eat any member of your family who dies in the city, and vultures will eat any who die in the countryside."
**25** There was never anyone who sold himself so completely to do evil in the LORD's sight as Ahab, urged on by his wife Jezebel.
**26** He behaved in the most detestable ways, worshiping idols just as the Amorites had done — the people the LORD had driven out before Israel.
**27** When Ahab heard these words, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, fasted, slept in sackcloth, and walked around subdued.
**28** Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah:
**29** "Have you noticed how Ahab has humbled himself before me? Because he has humbled himself, I will not bring this disaster during his lifetime. I will bring it on his family during his son's reign." 

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **21:3 — "my family's inheritance"**: Naboth is not being difficult. He is obeying Leviticus 25, which forbids permanent sale of ancestral land. The land belongs to God; families are stewards. Naboth's refusal is an act of covenant faithfulness against royal pressure.
2. **21:7 — "Is this how the king of Israel acts?"**: Jezebel's contempt is revealing. Where she comes from, kings don't ask — they take. Her question exposes the collision between Phoenician autocracy and Israelite covenant: in Israel, even the king is under the law. Jezebel is about to demonstrate what happens when a king stops believing that.
3. **21:19 — two crimes, one sentence**: Murder and theft. The Ten Commandments violated in a single real estate transaction. God doesn't separate the injustice from the property grab — they are one act with one judgment.
4. **21:27 — Ahab repents**: The worst king in Israel's history tears his clothes and puts on sackcloth. And God notices. This is one of the most startling moments in Kings: even Ahab's late, incomplete repentance moves God to postpone judgment. No one is too far gone for a divine second look.
5. **21:25 — "urged on by his wife"**: The narrator assigns Ahab the primary blame but names Jezebel as the catalyst. Together they are the most destructive partnership in Israelite history — he the willing puppet, she the strategic mastermind.

— PNEUMA
